payload.title: [LeftBlock] `leftblock ci`: run the repo's local CI command on an exact commit and issue a receipt (JSON + GitHub commit status)
payload.description:
Repo: DataParade-io/LeftBlock (public; ~/Projects/LeftBlock is read-only for agents: work in a fresh clone/worktree, PR to its default branch). Files: `leftblock/cli.py` (new subcommand), new `leftblock/ci.py`, `features/ci_receipt.feature` + steps, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

Configuration (`.leftblock.yml` in the adopting repo):
```yaml
ci:
  command: npm test            # one shell command; the repo decides what CI means
  status_context: leftblock/ci # GitHub status context
  sign: true                   # optional HMAC with the existing LEFTBLOCK_SECRET_PATH secret
```
Behaviour of `leftblock ci [--sha HEAD] [--no-status] [--dry-run]`:
1. Refuse unless the work tree is clean and `--sha` resolves to HEAD (the receipt is for exactly what was tested). Record `git rev-parse HEAD`, tree hash, `git describe --always`.
2. Run `ci.command` with output streamed; capture exit status, duration, start/end timestamps, tool versions (`node -v`, `python3 --version`, `leftblock --version`, and `git --version`).
3. Write receipt JSON to `.git/leftblock/receipts/<sha>.json`: `{sha, tree, checks:[{command, exit_code, duration_s}], result: "success"|"failure", started_at, finished_at, tools:{...}, leftblock_version, host, signature?: "hmac-sha256:<hex>"}`; signature = HMAC over `sha|tree|result|finished_at` with the shared secret (reuse `compute_hmac` shape in `leftblock/core.py`).
4. Post a commit status via `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/statuses/<sha> -f state=success|failure -f context=leftblock/ci -f description="<result> <n> checks <duration> sig:<first 12 hex>" -f target_url=` (gh resolves the repo from `origin`). Failure still posts `failure` so the deploy gate sees red. `--no-status` for offline runs.
5. Exit code mirrors the CI command.
Trust model (document in README): guards against mistakes (forgetting to run checks, deploying a red commit), not against a malicious committer; anyone with the gh token can post the status and anyone with the secret can sign. Optional signing lets the deploy gate verify the receipt was minted by a machine holding the secret.
Gherkin scenarios: clean tree success → status success + receipt; failing command → status failure, exit non-zero; dirty tree → refused; `--no-status` → receipt only. Tests with a fake `gh` on PATH.
